title: ElicitationTurnResponse
description: Normative shape of one turn the elicitation agent returns, for approval/contracts/rule-elicitation@0.1.0. The four-turn ceiling is held in the file as a bound on turnIndex rather than left to the agent's own discipline, because the failure it prevents is a conversation that never ends: the measured sessions reached turn 6 before converging (spikes/SP-2-rule-elicitation/REPORT.md section 1 Q4). By turn 3 the agent states the safest fail-closed reading rather than asking again, so a session that has run out of turns still leaves the user with something to accept or reject.

sessionId.description: The elicitation session this turn belongs to. Sessions are separate from jobs: nothing said here reaches a connector.

turnIndex.description: Which turn this is. The ceiling is in the file, so a fifth turn is not a long conversation but an inadmissible response (INV-AP-15).

agentInquiry.description: The question put to the user, carrying at most two points to clarify. Absent on a turn that presents a summary instead of asking.

summaryTable.description: The restatement offered for confirmation, shaped by rule-elicitation.schema.json. Present from turn 3 onward, and required on any turn that reports the conversation complete.

isComplete.description: Whether a summary is ready for the user to confirm. It does not mean a rule exists: a rule exists only once the user confirms what this turn showed them.

isRefused.description: Whether the intention as a whole could not be compiled. True here is a stated outcome, not a failure to answer: the user is told no hard rule can express what they said, and is pointed at smart approval mode instead of being given a rule that protects nothing.

refusalReason.description: Why the intention could not be compiled, in the user's own language. Required when isRefused is true, so a refusal is never a bare 'no'.
